title: How to Increase Salon Rebooking Rate (From 33% to 58%) — Lutily Blog

facts.fact: The industry average salon rebooking rate is around 40%, according to the article.
facts.quote: The industry average rebooking rate sits around **40%**.

facts.fact: The author's own salon had a rebooking rate of 33% when they pulled their numbers two years before writing the article.
facts.quote: Two years ago I pulled my numbers and found my rebook rate was **33%**.

facts.fact: A Boulevard industry report, as cited by the article, says most salons lose about 30% of their client base every year from natural attrition.
facts.quote: most salons lose about **30% of their client base every year** just from natural attrition.

facts.fact: According to Zenoti, as cited by the article, acquiring a new client costs five to twenty-five times more than keeping an existing one.
facts.quote: Acquiring a new client costs [five to twenty-five times more](https://www.zenoti.com/thecheckin/a-guide-to-salon-client-retention-8-essential-strategies) than keeping one you already have.

facts.fact: According to Phorest's retention data, as cited by the article, a returning client spends about 31% more per visit than a first-time client.
facts.quote: a returning client spends about **31% more per visit** than a first-timer, according to [Phorest’s retention data]

facts.fact: In the article's illustrative example, an average ticket of $85 and a client visiting every six weeks for three years is worth roughly $2,210 in total.
facts.quote: Say your average ticket is $85. A client who visits every six weeks for three years is worth roughly **$2,210**.

facts.fact: According to Savvy Salon Club, as cited by the article, tightening the average gap between visits from nine weeks to seven weeks produces a 29% increase in annual visits per client.
facts.quote: tightening the average gap between visits from nine weeks to seven weeks produces a **29% increase in annual visits per client**

facts.fact: In a Boulevard Client Retention Report, as cited by the article, top-performing salons convert 70% of first visits into a second appointment and 57% into a third.
facts.quote: Top-performing salons convert **70%** of first visits into a second appointment and **57%** into a third.

facts.fact: In the same Boulevard Client Retention Report, average salons convert 45% of first visits into a second appointment and 39% into a third.
According to Kitomba's industry data, as cited by the article, regular clients make up about 40% of the typical client base but account for 70% of all appointments.
facts.unit: % of client base and % of appointments
facts.quote: regular clients make up about **40% of the typical client base** but account for **70% of all appointments**.

facts.fact: In Boulevard's report, clients who book their first appointment online return for a second visit 78% of the time, versus 39% for walk-ins.
facts.quote: clients who book their first appointment **online** return for a second visit **78% of the time**. Walk-ins return at just **39%**.

facts.fact: In Boulevard's report, 54% of online-booked clients reach a third visit, compared with 25% of walk-in clients.
The article states that clients who request a specific stylist when booking online spend 30% more per visit than clients who request no one.
facts.quote: clients who request a specific stylist when booking online spend **30% more per visit** than clients who don’t request anyone.

facts.fact: The article's narrator and personal experiences are fictional, as stated in an editorial disclaimer.
facts.quote: The narrator and personal experiences described are fictional.
